summary: Can trading 12-month trends in macro fundamentals (growth, inflation, trade, monetary policy, risk aversion) earn returns like price trend? Directional futures backtest 1970-2022 across 59 equity, bond, STIR, FX and commodity markets with fixed theory-based signs, equal risk, 10% vol. Economic trend: Sharpe 1.1, ~0 correlation to stocks/bonds, strong in their drawdowns; 50/50 with price trend (corr 0.4) lifts Sharpe to 1.5.

claims.speaker: authors

reasoning.question: Can an investor earn trend-following-like returns by positioning each equity, bond, rate, currency and commodity market on trends in macro fundamentals (growth, inflation, trade, monetary policy, risk aversion) instead of past prices, and does this diversify stocks, bonds and price trend, especially in drawdowns? It matters because trend-following is held mainly as drawdown protection and price trend alone fails in sharp reversals.

thesis.statement: Because markets underreact to economic news, trading 12-month trends in five macro themes with theory-fixed signs earned a Sharpe ratio of about 1.1 (1970-2022, gross) with near-zero stock/bond correlation and gains in their worst drawdowns; capturing the same underreaction through different inputs, it is only moderately correlated with price trend (0.4), so a 50/50 blend (Sharpe 1.5) beats either alone in return and drawdown protection.

foundations.premise: Asset prices systematically underreact to new information, so news is incorporated gradually and creates trends.
foundations.support: citations: time series momentum evidence over 120+ years and single-stock underreaction studies; extended to index and bond markets by two studies

foundations.premise: Underreaction has behavioural causes (biased belief updating, herding, extrapolation, disposition effect).
foundations.support: citations to theory papers (Barberis-Shleifer-Vishny, Daniel-Hirshleifer-Subrahmanyam, Hong-Stein, Frazzini); not tested here

foundations.premise: For macro assets, the relevant news is mostly news about economic fundamentals, so price trends are only an indirect and sometimes misleading proxy for it.
Each theme has a stable, 'other things equal' sign of effect on each asset class (e.g. rising growth good for equities, rising inflation bad for bonds and good for the currency).
foundations.support: economic channels with citations (cash flows, Balassa-Samuelson, Katz-Lustig, Clarida-Waldman, Bernanke-Kuttner, Eichenbaum-Evans, Campbell); said to be 'empirically verified' contemporaneously but no test is shown

foundations.premise: If news has a persistent impact, the predictive sign of a news trend must equal its contemporaneous sign, so imposing that restriction limits data mining.
Twelve-month changes in consensus forecasts (or, before 1991, realized data lagged one quarter, equivalent under a random walk) measure the news investors receive.
foundations.support: assertion; random-walk equivalence stated, not tested

foundations.premise: Large stock and bond drawdowns rarely come out of the blue; they are usually preceded by deteriorating fundamentals (growth, hawkish policy).
Prices can stay disconnected from fundamentals for prolonged periods (bubbles), and later re-couple.
Investors value trend-following mainly for positive returns in market drawdowns.
Simple, long-history measures are less exposed to data mining, and a simple backtest understates what a richer real-time signal set could achieve.

reasoning.forward_looking_inputs: (reader) Observable inputs: 12-month changes in consensus real GDP and CPI forecasts, 12-month change in the export-weighted exchange rate, 12-month change in 2-year yields, and the equal mix of 12-month equity excess return and credit-spread change, per country (consumption-weighted for commodities), mapped by the Exhibit 1 signs. Through step 2 (underreaction) they are said to lead returns of equity index, bond, short-rate, currency and commodity futures over the following months (monthly rebalanced; the decay horizon of the edge is not measured). They would stop working if markets absorbed macro news faster (more capital in macro systematic strategies), if prices stay decoupled from fundamentals for long periods (bubbles), if the sign map breaks (e.g. a change in the stock-bond correlation regime or in central bank credibility changes how inflation news moves equities, bonds and currencies), or in low macro-volatility periods like the 2010s.
reader_inferences: (reader) Rebalancing is monthly; the paper reports monthly returns but never states the trading frequency.
(reader) Positions appear to be taken by direction of the theme change; whether signal magnitude scales positions is not stated.
(reader) The monetary policy sign text in the appendix is likely a wording slip; Exhibit 1 and economic logic should be trusted.

(reader) Equity momentum in the risk aversion theme and the trade theme in currencies make part of 'economic trend' a price-based signal, which may account for some of the correlation with price trend.
(reader) Drawdown evidence is based on five ex-post chosen episodes per asset and overlaps with inflation shocks, so it is suggestive, not conclusive.
(reader) The 2017-2022 out-of-sample result is concentrated in one inflation-and-tightening regime (short stocks and bonds 2020-2022).
(reader) Pre-1991 realized-data signals may contain revised data that was not known at the time, adding look-ahead not discussed in the paper.
(reader) Sign stability across regimes (e.g. positive vs negative stock-bond correlation eras) is an untested assumption of the fixed sign map.
(reader) Net-of-cost performance is unknown; the low-turnover claim is not quantified.
